newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLS ROMP PAST MAGIC.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-BULLS ROMP PAST MAGIC.

text.p: Scottie Pippen had 22 points, 11 assists and six steals and Michael Jordan added 19 points, 10 assists and eight rebounds as the Chicago Bulls breezed to a 110-89 victory over the Orlando Magic on Sunday.
Toni Kukoc added 20 points for the Bulls, who have won three in a row and 28 of 31, extending their league-best record to 45-6.
The Bulls never trailed after a free throw by Dennis Rodman gave them a 3-2 lead less than two minutes into the game and led by as many as 26 points.
In Los Angeles, Gary Payton's layup with 2:12 left ignited a game-ending 13-2 run and lifted the Seattle SuperSonics to a 102-91 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers.

Detlef Schrempf scored a season-high 34 points on 14-of-18 shooting and Payton had 19 of his 21 points in the second half for Seattle, which moved within 1-1/2 games of the first-place Lakers in the Western Conference.

"I don't know if it's that big of a win," said Sonics coach George Karl. "It's still the middle of the season. We're in a marathon. Rhythm and tempo, injuries and maybe a trade will determine what's going to happen."
In New York, the New York Knicks held Indiana to one field goal in the fourth quarter and rallied from a 19-point deficit to defeat the Pacers, 89-80.

"It was a great, great comeback," said Knicks coach Jeff Van Gundy. "The defence was good the entire second half, but the offence was poor until the fourth quarter. We played a championship calibre fourth quarter, but we have to do it for four quarters."

Indiana stormed to a 34-15 lead in the first half and took a 12-point advantage into the fourth quarter. But the Pacers hit just 1-of-15 shots and star guard Reggie Miller scored just three points in the final quarter.

In Philadelphia, LaPhonso Ellis scored 18 of his career-high 37 points in the first quarter as the Denver Nuggets raced to a 13-point lead and defeated the Philadelphia 76ers 112-97 to end a three-game losing streak.
Antonio McDyess had 21 points and 11 rebounds and Mark Jackson had 14 points and 14 assists for Denver. Jackson led the team in assists for the 33rd consecutive game.

In Sacramento, Mitch Richmond became the 74th player in NBA history to score 15,000 points, and Olden Polynice had 23 points and 10 rebounds as the Sacramento Kings routed the Golden State Warriors 105-85.
Richmond, who needed to 15 points to reach the milestone, scored 19, including the historic three-pointer with 2:53 left in the game.
Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf scored 18 of his 22 points in the second half and added eight assists as the Kings scored 63 points after halftime.
In Toronto, Joe Dumars scored nine of his 15 points in the last two minutes as the Detroit Pistons remained perfect against the slumping Toronto Raptors with a 92-89 victory at Maple Leaf Gardens.
Grant Hill had 23 points and 18 rebounds for the Pistons, who overcame a 17-point, second-quarter deficit to win.
"I don't think I've ever had that many rebounds, but it was a team focus to control the boards," Hill said.
Walt Williams scored 22 points for Toronto.

At Minnesota, Tom Gugliotta scored 23 points and Kevin Garnett and Stephon Marbury led second-half surges as the Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the Phoenix Suns for the third time this season, 107-96.

Garnett scored 10 of his 21 points in a rally that opened the third quarter and erased an eight-point halftime deficit. Marbury, who had 15 points and nine assists, made a clutch three-pointer and a layup off a steal down the stretch.

In Portland, Isaiah Rider scored a season-high 40 points and Rasheed Wallace added six of his 22 points in a second-quarter run as the Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Boston Celtics, 118-106, for their third win in four games.
Gary Trent had 19 points and 10 rebounds and Kenny Anderson had 13 points and nine assists for Portland.
